name: el_symbols_at
description: Symbol library of the electrical editor. One home for every symbol: the palette, the placed symbols, the print legend and the Documentation tab all read it from here (vpt/el_symbols.py checks it; the editor build fails when it is broken). More than one set may be listed; the page then lets the user pick the set (default_set first).

sets.standard: ÖVE/ÖNORM EN 60617 (graphical symbols for diagrams; the part with the symbols for installation plans)
sets.installation_standard: OVE E 8101 (low-voltage electrical installations in Austria)
sets.edition: not checked: the symbols were drawn without the standard text, so no edition can be claimed
sets.provenance: Drawn for the vienna_planning_toolkit by Claude (an AI assistant) from general knowledge of the IEC 60617 installation-plan conventions as used on German and Austrian plans. Plain lines, arcs and letters only. Not copied from any file, website or catalogue, and not checked against the standard text.
sets.status: UNVERIFIED — not yet checked against the standard text or the Elektroplaner
sets.to_verify: Obtain the symbol table of ÖVE/ÖNORM EN 60617 (installation-plan symbols) or the Elektroplaner's legend, compare every symbol, then set verified to true and verified_against to the document and edition for each symbol that matches (and redraw the ones that do not).
sets.units: Millimetres on the storey sheet (the architect's plan at its print scale). The symbol's insertion point is 0,0; +y (down) is the wall side: a socket's stem points to the wall it sits on. Rotation turns the symbol about 0,0.

symbols.note: Luminaire, general: a circle with a cross.
The luminaire symbol with a bar on the wall side; the bar convention is the least certain part.
A small circle with one stroke and one hook.
Two strokes in opposite directions, each with a hook (point-symmetric). Used in pairs: one light from two places.
Four strokes with hooks. Sits between two two-way switches: one light from three or more places.
A circle with a smaller circle inside (e.g. for a stairwell timer or an impulse relay).
The general socket outlet: an arc and a stem to the wall. In Austria sockets normally have a protective contact (Schuko): use SS1 unless the plan says otherwise.
The socket outlet with a line across the arc for the protective contact.
